thread.title: How Can Apple Recover When Its Business Model Limits Growth? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Edward Ambrose
title: How Can Apple Recover When Its Business Model Limits Growth? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Apple Stock Price
Source Finbox.io
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) stock has fallen 35% in three months but so have its prospects. I recommended the purchase of Apple because I believed that the higher revenue per phone would offset the lower unit sales. That was true in the United States and other developed countries but not in China or India. This brings up the fundamental tradeoffs in their business model that make growth more difficult. Apple spends $14 billion per year on product development. The productivity of this spending has declined, as ventures into TV and the HomePods developed slower than competition, so they entered crowded markets. The stock is a sell.
Holiday Quarter performance Tim Cook's letter to shareholders indicates that net income will be $20 billion and that earnings per share will be above four dollars despite the disappointing iPhone sales in China. So, is the crisis overblown? Unfortunately, no. The table below demonstrates that revenue is down 4.9% and operating income down 12% from prior year. The tax cut and stock buybacks have improved the earnings per share, but these were factored into the stock valuation. The fall in revenue and operating income was a shock.
Business Model Apple's gross profit on the iPhone is around 50-70% - an astronomical number. Apple has engineered the iPhone for low-cost production reducing the number of chips, consolidating functions and eliminating expensive suppliers like Qualcomm ( QCOM ). Teardown numbers are very rough, and they do not take into account the software development and engineering, but the numbers are still astronomical.
An iPhone buyer can get a lower priced android phone, but Apple gained share in the developed world. An iPhone user will not want to learn the ins and outs of a different smartphone. The iPhone human factors are excellent, but it is not just that. The iPhone connects to the iCloud. Apple computers work better with the iPhone. There is iTunes and Apple Pay. Apple apps are 40% of the $11 billion service revenue.
A buyer of the Apple XS or XR can upgrade from an older model paying a higher monthly fee. Therefore, they do not see the upfront cost of the iPhone. The older model is refurbished and put back into service growing the base of Apple users.
This is a model for making high profits from an existing base. In China, the base of existing iPhone users is small. Phone companies do not finance the phone purchases on a monthly fee. Therefore, they have to go head to head with a technologically advanced phone sold with a low margin. Apple also plans on $5 billion from India this year. That is looking increasingly unlikely.
Pricing Revenue per iPhone shown below was up 29% in 2018 fiscal 4th quarter. It is about 15% higher in the first quarter. With high prices, the volume goes down. Apple cut prices of the iPhone 7 and 8, offering a good value from a technical perspective. However, Apple is a luxury brand. The lowest price new phone with the new image was the XR at $749. This phone was too expensive to sell in the volume Apple projected.
New Product Development Apple spends $14 billion annually on product development. They are attempting to build the web of connected businesses to make the iPhone even more indispensable. The iWatch is an example of this. Apple is building a patient medical records system, which could take input from devices like the iWatch.
Other examples are the Apple TV and the HomePod, which integrate into the Apple ecosystem. However, these ventures did not achieve a strong market position before the competition, which has much lower cost devices from Roku and Amazon ( AMZN ). For this to work, Apple needs to be a clear leader, as is the iWatch. Expansion into medical devices and services is promising, but they will take time to develop.
5G The 5G system allows data transmission at very high speed. Therefore, a phone needs a modem that can function with the high-speed data as well as existing speeds. This will probably change the smartphone features. So, the display can be 8K rather than 4K. A higher quality camera may be more important. The 5G systems will start to be significant beginning in 2020. Apple would like to have phones that are compatible with 5G next fall because no one wants an expensive phone that suddenly becomes obsolete. Intel (NASDAQ: INTC ), the current manufacturer of iPhone modems, has moved the 5G phone modem up six months to the last half of 2019 for 2020 deliveries. If Apple waits, it would lose its best quarter for iPhone sales.
The higher speed 5G will be helpful to Apple in selling new phones. The risk to Apple is that the existing phones become less attractive with lower trade in value.
2019 Product Introductions Apple needs an iPhone that looks like the XR but at a lower price. The trick is to bring out a lower priced iPhone that minimizes the cannibalization of sales of the higher priced models. A version with the smaller size of the 6SE is possible but not probable. Apple TV has new shows available for streaming. They will probably bring out a lower cost TV on a stick and introduce a streaming service as Amazon did, but the profits from being a follower are mediocre. A smaller iPad and some accessories can be expected alone with a lower priced HomePod. Nothing except a better-priced iPhone will produce growth for Apple in 2019.
Conclusions The holidays are the peak season for iPhone sales, but the new XR was too expensive to build the base of users of Apple services. The lack of 5G could lower the effect of fall iPhone introduction. Apple has an aggressive plan for trade-ups through the Apple Stores. It will probably make the XR at lower cost through discounts through mobile phone networks. At the end of January, Apple will provide guidance for the full year. It is unlikely to be good news. Apple is a sell.
